name: Jotham
source_summary: King of Judah who governed as regent during his father Uzziah's leprosy-enforced isolation, then reigned in his own right, strengthening Jerusalem's defenses and defeating the Ammonites, remembered as doing right yet unable to remove the high places.
family_friendly_summary: Jotham became king of Judah after ruling for a while as his father Uzziah's helper, since Uzziah had a skin disease that kept him from entering the temple or ruling in public. Jotham did what was right in the LORD's eyes, following his father's good example. He built the upper gate of the temple, strengthened cities and forts, and led Judah to defeat the Ammonites, who then paid Judah tribute for several years. But even though Jotham himself was a good king, most of the people of Judah kept living in ways that did not honor God, and the high places used for false worship were never removed.
adult_story: Jotham, son of Uzziah and Jerusha, governed Judah as regent while his father lived isolated with leprosy after Uzziah's unlawful attempt to burn incense in the temple (2 Kings 15:5; 2 Chronicles 26:16-21). At twenty-five, Jotham became king in his own right and reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem, doing "right in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his father Uzziah had done" (2 Kings 15:32-34). He built the upper gate of the temple, did extensive construction on the wall of Ophel, and built cities in the hill country of Judah along with forts and towers in the forests (2 Chronicles 27:3-4). He made war against the king of the Ammonites and prevailed, and for three years the Ammonites paid him a heavy annual tribute of silver, wheat, and barley (27:5). Scripture credits his strength directly to his obedience: "he ordered his ways before the LORD his God" (27:6). Yet the record is not uncritical -- "the people continued acting corruptly," and, as under his father, the high places used for unauthorized worship were not removed (2 Kings 15:35). His reign overlaps the ministries of the prophets Isaiah, Hosea, and Micah, and he appears in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus as an ancestor of the Messiah (Matthew 1:9).

devotionals: Jotham governed faithfully, ordering his ways before God, yet the high places he inherited were never removed. Jesus alone finishes the reform every faithful king left undone.

reign.note: 2 Kings 15:33 states Jotham reigned sixteen years, a count most chronologies read as including a co-regency with his father Uzziah during Uzziah's years of leprous isolation.
